title: Evidence package and operational sign-off for private keying, audit and SSO readiness
creator: Evelyn Park
description:
Summary: Compile a complete evidence package and operational sign-off path for Private deployments focusing on SSO/SAML assertion fidelity, RBAC scoping, immutable audit logging, and KMS/HSM key custody. This ticket coordinates PM acceptance criteria, ops runbook updates, and legal/compliance artifact generation for customer onboarding.

Scope Clarifications / Decisions so far: 
- We will require SAML 2.0 with signed assertions and support for both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. Decision: support for multiple IdP certificates via JWK set URL (ops will rotate certs via the console).
- RBAC model: adopt 'role + resource scope' model used by internal console with two new cluster-scoped roles: private_admin (full deploy lifecycle) and audit_reader (read-only access to audit logs). Decision: map existing org-role matrix to these new roles for Private installs.
- Audit logs: immutable append-only storage backed by object storage with write-once lifecycle tag. Logs must include request metadata, token reference (redacted), model and route, and keying events (KMS operations).
- KMS/HSM: support two modes: customer-managed KMS (BYOK via external cloud KMS with key-resident HSM) and Redwood-managed HSM with tenant-specific key partitions. Acceptance requires proof of key-wrapping and rotation (see checklist).

Trade-offs considered: 
- Full key custody (customer KMS only) increases onboarding friction — we chose to support both modes to maximize enterprise adoption.
- Real-time log forwarding to customer SIEM may add latency; we will provide batch export and streaming via Kafka connector as opt-in.

Artifacts to attach to evidence package: PRD (Confluence: /display/PRD/Private+Keying+Audit+2025), Ops runbook (Drive: /drive/ops/private-keying-runbook-v2.pdf), Demo script, compliance checklist spreadsheet, sample SBOM for the private bundle, GH PRs and runtime test traces.

Acceptance process: PM verifies runbook + test outputs -> Security team performs threat review -> Compliance signs off on evidence -> Eng closes release gating ticket. Each step requires documented artifacts linked below.

Open questions: 
- Should we require HSM attestation from vendor during onboarding (ATT 1)? (security requested, ops requests a staged approach).
- How strict should SSO session TTL mapping be between IdP and Redwood tokens? (Ops suggests 1:1 mapping as default with override by customer policy).
acceptance_criteria: SSO: Support for SAML 2.0 signed assertions with JWK URL certificate rotation; IdP and SP-initiated flows validated in staging
RBAC: Two cluster roles (private_admin, audit_reader) implemented with example mappings; role assignment documented in runbook
Audit logs: Immutable append-only storage proven via test vectors; sample log entries include timestamp, actor-id, route, model id, and key operation events
KMS: Both BYOK and Redwood-managed HSM modes demonstrable; key wrap/unwrap and rotation recorded in audit logs
Evidence package: PRD, runbook, compliance checklist, exportable sample logs, and signed security review attached to ticket
Onboarding playbook: Step-by-step customer onboarding checklist with manual validation steps and automated tests
Sign-offs: Security, Compliance, and Solutions Engineering approvals captured as linked artifacts
Operational alerts: Alert rules defined for failed key rotations, SSO assertion validation failures, and audit log ingestion gaps
